titleStmt.title: Memorandum From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (McFarlane) to Secretary of State Shultz, Secretary of the Treasury James Baker, and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (Stockman)

div.head: 384. Memorandum From the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (McFarlane) to Secretary of State Shultz, Secretary of the Treasury James Baker, and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (Stockman)
div.p: I have been impressed with the free market economic policies developed by Ecuadorean President Febres-Cordero and believe we have a stake in the success of his programs because of the positive influence this would have on other Latin American Countries. I believe that the political support President Febres-Cordero has given to us has also been helpful on issues that are important to US interests—Central America, Cuba, and the increasingly politicized approach to the debt problem. (S)

In terms of strict economic need, Ecuador might not seem in as great a need for American help as other countries. Yet, I believe, that from time to time, it is both a legitimate and effective use of US power to send political signals to governments that are in sync with US goals and values. The Government of Ecuador fulfills that criteria. They have requested that we assist them, and I believe that ESF funding is appropriate for their current needs. (C)

I would appreciate it if the ad hoc group, chaired by William Schneider, that was established to deal with this type of problem could be promptly convened to explore the possibility of securing FY 1985 ESF for Ecuador. (C)

note.p: Source: Reagan Library, NSC Records, Latin American Affairs Directorate, Country File, Ecuador (04/03/1985–08/01/1985). Secret. A copy was sent to Bush. An unknown hand wrote at the top of the page: “Help for Febres.” Bush wrote at the top of the page: “I strongly concur!! GB 7–31.” Tillman sent the memo to McFarlane under cover of a July 18 memorandum, in which she wrote: “I have felt for some time that it is a legitimate and effective use of US power to send political signals to countries and governments that are in sync with US goals and values. Money is such a signal, and Ecuador is infinitely deserving.” Tillman also noted: “Febres-Cordero’s economic program—he’s doing all the right things, and his success will encourage other Latins to consider implementing similar economic policies. And, as a conservative, he is and will continue to be helpful to us on issues ranging from Central America, Cuba, and the politicization of the debt issue.”
Bush drew a checkmark on the left-hand margin next to “positive influence.”
Bush drew a line along this paragraph on the left-hand margin and underlined: “explore the possibility of securing FY1985 ESF for Ecuador.”
McFarlane signed the memorandum “Bud McFarlane” above his typed signature.
